chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding the man who settles another man in his house, and [the right is] for his offspring after him, he (peace be upon him) said: 'It is permissible, and it is not for them to sell it, nor to inherit it.' I said, 'So a man settles a man in his house for his lifetime?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'That is permissible.' I said, 'So a man settles a man in his house and does not stipulate a time period?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'It is permissible, and he can evict him whenever he wishes.'
ai.seo_question: What are the legal conditions for granting someone the right to live in a house without transferring ownership?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the flexibility of habitation grants (sukna) by permitting residence for a lifetime or heirs, while explicitly prohibiting the sale or inheritance of the property itself to preserve the donor's intent. The ruling further establishes that indefinite habitation grants remain revocable at the donor's discretion, reflecting the Shia juristic distinction between usufruct rights and full ownership in charitable endowments.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hamaad, from Al Halby,

(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> regarding the man who settles the man in his house, and for it to be for his offspring from after him. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He is allowed, and it is not for them that they should sell it, nor for it to be inherited’. I said, ‘So a man settles a man in his house for his lifetime?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He is allowed that’. I said, ‘So a man settles a man in his house and does not stipulate a time period?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Allowed, and he can vacate him whenever he so desires to’.
en.sarwar: 25. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Flammad from al-Halabiy who has narrated the following: “

I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a man who allows another man to use a house and those whom he will leave behind. He (the Imam) said, ‘It is permissible but they cannot sell or inherit it.’ I asked if a man could allow another man to use a house for his lifetime. He (the Imam) said, ‘It is permissible.’ I then asked what happens if a man allows another man to use a house without the mention of time. He (the Imam) said, ‘It is permissible but he can ask him to vacate if he wants.’”
